title: Kaboom Crew lighting + shadow + autotile integration — first showcase of the visual fidelity refresh
intent: After GDP-001 (lighting engine), GDP-002 (Wang autotile engine), GDP-003 (per-tile variants) ship as engine + project content, this story stitches them all together inside Kaboom Crew. Result: default arena has directional shadow casting from upper-left, soft+hard block walls visibly connected via Wang autotile selection, bombs near detonation glow with attached point lights that cast brief shadows of nearby blocks. Single-sprint integration story that closes the visual fidelity refresh. Showcases the engine's new capabilities in the flagship sample — exactly the role Kaboom Crew is for.
rationale: Source: memory [project-visual-fidelity-evolution] + user request 2026-05-28 'тени, источники света и прочие эффекты + различные материалы для тайлов + wang tiles'. This is the project-side adoption of the three engine modules (lighting + Wang + variants) — without this story, the engine work has no visible payoff. Per CLAUDE.md engine-first philosophy, engine ships generic; project consumes. Sized `should` because the engine prerequisites are themselves `should` — the visible win lands when this lands.
acceptanceHints: DEPENDS ON ALL THREE: GDP-2026-05-28-001 (lighting engine), GDP-2026-05-28-002 (Wang autotile engine), GDP-2026-05-28-003 (per-tile variants). Can ship in stages: variants-only (no autotile, no shadows) is the v1 showcase; lighting-only is the v2; full integration is the v3. Each stage produces visible improvement.
STAGE 1 — TILE VARIANTS WITH RANDOM SELECTION (depends on GDP-003 only):
examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts: load the 4 hard-block + 4 soft-block + 4 floor-tile procedural mesh variants at boot. Replace single-mesh refs in scene loader with per-cell hash-based selection.
Arenas immediately look more varied. No autotile yet.
STAGE 2 — LIGHTING + SHADOWS (depends on GDP-001):
examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts: register a directional key light (intensity 1.0, color cream-tinted #f4ede0, castShadow true, shadowMapSize 2048, position above-arena upper-left).
Existing ambient + hemispheric stay.
Tag all bomber meshes + bomb mesh + soft-block + hard-block as ShadowCaster.
Tag arena floor + hard blocks + soft blocks as ShadowReceiver.

Bomb-fuse-system (or a sibling) attaches a point light to each bomb when fuseRemaining < 0.6s (final-fuse window). Light: red #ff4040, intensity 1.5, castShadow false (cheap), follows bomb position. Light despawns on detonation.
Pickup mesh entities attach a soft point light: cyan #33ffff, intensity 0.3, castShadow false, ambient glow.
STAGE 3 — WANG AUTOTILE (depends on GDP-002):

examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts: register 3 Wang tile families using the variant builders from GDP-003 as Wang variant content. Each family has 16 variants — variant builders from GDP-003 take an optional `bitmask` parameter; map the 16 Wang indices to 4 base shape variants via a 16→4 lookup table that picks visually-coherent shapes per bitmask.
Example soft-block lookup table:
bitmask 0 (isolated) → variant 3 (drum — looks like a single object).
bitmask 1,2,4,8 (single-neighbour) → variant 0 (crate — looks like 'edge of wall').
bitmask 3,5,6,9,10,12 (two-neighbour) → variant 1 (pallet — looks like 'corner').
bitmask 7,11,13,14 (three-neighbour) → variant 1 (pallet — looks like 'T-junction').
bitmask 15 (surrounded) → variant 2 (barrel-corner — looks like 'wall filler').
Hard-block + floor-tile families use similar lookup tables.
WangTile-tagged scene entities replace the random-per-cell selection from Stage 1.
Block destruction event triggers re-resolve on the 4 cardinal neighbours of the destroyed cell.
EXISTING TESTS:
bot-vs-bot.test.ts continues to resolve in budget (visual changes don't affect gameplay).
Existing arena scene tests pass with the new mesh paths.
Existing recording fixture (recordings/demo-30s.recording.json) regenerated — gameplay events identical, visual frames will differ.
PERFORMANCE:
Directional shadow @ 2048: ~3ms / frame.
2 point lights w/o shadows: ~0.5ms.
Wang resolver: 0ms steady-state (only on scene-load + block events).
Tile variant count: same draw call count as before (instanced where possible).
Total perf budget impact: ~4ms / frame at peak, well within 16.6ms (60fps) budget per visual-style.md §11.
DOCS UPDATES (in this PR):
examples/kaboom-crew/README.md — visual showcase section noting shadows + lit pickups + autotile arenas.
visual-style.md — replace any lingering 'no shadow maps' / 'single light' wording with the new state.
ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST:
Load default arena. Cast shadows visible from bombers + bombs + blocks under the directional light. Pickups subtly glow cyan. Final-fuse bombs glow red with brief shadow flicker.
Soft-block wall (5+ adjacent soft blocks): visibly looks like a CONNECTED wall, not 5 separate bricks. Corners + edges + interior cells have distinct mesh.
Destroy a soft block mid-wall: the 4 neighbours visually update — old corner pieces become new corner pieces matching the new neighbourhood.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Per-arena theme switching (warehouse/factory/lab/etc themes from visual-style.md §9.2). Single 'default' theme for now; theme system is a follow-up.
Animated shadow tweens (e.g. shadow softness changes with bomb-pulse). Static shadow params.
Multi-light dancing on big chain reactions (each blast attaches a point light). Out — would overload the 4-light point budget; could re-evaluate later.
Sub-variant random variation within a Wang index (Wang index uniquely picks one mesh in v1).
